summary: Biblios is a quick, elegant filler about bidding on and drafting cards representing manuscripts, scribes, and resources needed to win five separate scoring categories. Its two-phase structure — a card-passing draft followed by blind auctions — makes for tense, fast decisions with a strong push-your-luck feel.
praised: Fast, elegant design that teaches in minutes
Clever two-phase structure combining drafting and bidding
Plays very well at two players and scales cleanly
criticised: Significant luck from the initial card reveal and God's Favor phase
Low strategic depth compared to heavier auction games
Can feel too random for players wanting more control

interaction.detail: Players bid against each other for the same cards during the market phase and compete directly for majority control in each of the five categories. The card marketplace and gold reserves are shared/visible state, while each player's collected cards and coins form their own hidden holdings until scoring.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is decided by who holds the majority in the most of five categories (illuminators, scribes, manuscripts, scrolls, supplies), so category control matters more than raw point totals.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by securing majority holdings in more of the five card categories than any other player, using careful bidding and drafting to outmaneuver rivals.
